newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea to consider sending aid to North if asked.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea to consider sending aid to North if asked.

text.p: South Korea will consider sending food aid to famine-striken North Korea if an international group makes a formal appeal, a spokesman for the Unification Ministry said on Monday.

"We have not decided what the item will be, how much it will be, or when and how the aid will be sent," he said. "But we will positively consider sending aid if an appeal is made by international organisations."
The United Nation's World Food Program (WFP) is expected to make the appeal this week, U.S. State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns said last week.
He sent a strong signal that Washington was willing to help Pyongyang with its food problems.
"I would remind you that we have responded positively to every previous appeal by the World Food Programme in the last year or two," Burns told reporters on Thursday.

In an interview with CNN on Thursday, the North Korean ambassador to the U.N. said a briefing on the U.S.-South Korean proposal for Korean peace talks had been delayed because Washington had not carried out a promise to provide food aid.
After North Korea apologised for a September submarine infiltration into South Korea, Washington gave U.S. grain exporter Cargill Inc permission to barter 500,000 tonnes of grain with North Korea.
Pyongyang has not yet been able to close the deal.
The grain shipment would help North Korea, which is suffering from acute food shortages caused by massive floods in 1995 and 1996.
The South Korean Red Cross in February made two aid shipments involving a total of 1,000 tonnes of flour and 15,000 pairs of socks.
The South Korean government provided $3.0 million in aid to North Korea through the WFP last year, while Washington provided $8.2 million.
